13	# ADR-013: `claude-tui` PTY Harness as a Fork of `claude`
14	
15	| Date | Status | Deciders | Related | Confidence |
16	|------|--------|----------|---------|------------|
17	| 2026-05-14 | **Withdrawn** pending [ADR-014](./ADR-014-universal-harness-interface.md) / [CONTRACT-004](../contracts/CONTRACT-004-harness-implementation.md) | Fizeau maintainers | ADR-002, ADR-004, ADR-011, ADR-014, CONTRACT-004 | Medium |
18	
19	> **Status note (2026-05-14):** This ADR is withdrawn pending the
20	> universal harness interface refactor in
21	> [ADR-014](./ADR-014-universal-harness-interface.md) and
22	> [CONTRACT-004](../contracts/CONTRACT-004-harness-implementation.md).
23	> A 2026-05-14 inventory found 69 service-side call sites reaching into
24	> per-harness exports beyond the documented `Harness` interface;
25	> introducing `claude-tui` against that surface would either duplicate
26	> ~25 exports under a new prefix or wire service code through a fifth
27	> set of per-harness imports. Both outcomes are the leak pattern
28	> CONTRACT-004 exists to eliminate.
29	>
30	> The fork remains the right shape for accessing Anthropic subscription
31	> pricing through the TUI. Re-proposal happens after CONTRACT-004
32	> merges, at which point the implementation reduces to: a new
33	> `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/` package implementing
34	> `Harness` + `QuotaHarness` + `AccountHarness` +
35	> `ModelDiscoveryHarness`, sharing a snapshot type with `claude`
36	> through an `internal/harnesses/anthropic/` neutral subpackage. No
37	> service-side changes required.
38	>
39	> The companion implementation plan
40	> [`plan-2026-05-14-claude-tui-fork.md`](../plan-2026-05-14-claude-tui-fork.md)
41	> is superseded by
42	> [`plan-2026-05-14-harness-interface-refactor.md`](../plan-2026-05-14-harness-interface-refactor.md)
43	> for the prerequisite refactor work. A new claude-tui plan is written
44	> after re-proposal.
45	>
46	> The capability-baseline row added by this ADR
47	> (`claude-tui` in `primary-harness-capability-baseline.md`) and the
48	> recorder reference in `harness-golden-integration.md` are removed
49	> alongside this status flip.
50	>
51	> ---
52	>
53	> ### Prior art surveyed (2026-05-14)
54	>
55	> Two reference implementations exist for driving Claude Code outside
56	> the `claude --print` batch path. Future re-proposal does not have to
57	> redo this survey.
58	>
59	> | Project | Transport | Session lifetime | Notes |
60	> |---------|-----------|------------------|-------|
61	> | [smithersai/claude-p](https://github.com/smithersai/claude-p) | in-process PTY (zmux) + `--settings '<inline-json>'` to register `SessionStart`/`Stop` hooks | per-invocation, one-shot | A small ANSI scanner answers Ink's DA1/DA2/DSR/XTVERSION/window-size startup probes — no full terminal emulator. Final text + usage extracted by reading the JSONL transcript whose path is delivered in the `Stop` hook payload. README explicitly notes "client-side restrictions ... are fundamentally unenforceable"; no claim about subscription billing. |
62	> | [dexhorthy/shannon](https://github.com/dexhorthy/shannon) | tmux session + `tmux send-keys` | persistent across turns | Reads the same JSONL transcript by tailing `~/.claude/projects/`. Rejected as a transport choice for Fizeau per ADR-002 (tmux is not part of the core path), but informative as convergent evidence for the parsing seam. |
63	>
64	> The convergent insight from both projects: **the parsing seam is the
65	> on-disk JSONL transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<workdir>/<id>.jsonl`,
66	> not rendered TUI output, regardless of transport choice**.
67	> `internal/pty/terminal` frame derivation and screen pattern-matching
68	> are not required for normal prompt execution under either reference
69	> design; they remain required only for the `/usage` quota probe.
70	>
71	> ### Design direction for re-proposal
72	>
73	> The following decisions are recorded here so the future ADR-013
74	> re-proposer can adopt them without re-deriving the rationale. They
75	> are constraints, not interface contract — CONTRACT-004 and ADR-014
76	> remain unaffected and transport-agnostic.
77	>
78	> 1. **Transport**: in-process PTY via the existing `internal/pty/`
79	>    library, with hooks registered via `--settings '<inline-json>'`
80	>    (Anthropic-published extension point). The `--settings` flag is
81	>    explicitly distinguished from the previously-forbidden batch flags
82	>    (`--print`, `-p`, `--output-format`, `--stream-json`, `--effort`,
83	>    `--model`, `--permission-mode`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`)
84	>    because it configures end-user-facing behavior the way a user's
85	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` would, not an automation/batch mode. The
86	>    batch-flag prohibition stands; the `--settings` carve-out is
87	>    additive.
88	>
89	> 2. **Output parsing**: read the JSONL transcript whose path is
90	>    delivered in the `Stop` hook payload. Do not parse rendered TUI
91	>    output. `internal/pty/terminal` (vt10x) is not required for
92	>    Execute; the PTY layer is reduced to "enough to keep Ink happy at
93	>    startup" — a small responder for DA1 / DA2 / DSR / XTVERSION /
94	>    window-size probes. A reusable startup-probe responder belongs in
95	>    `internal/pty/` so the quota probe path can consume it too.
96	>
97	> 3. **Streaming progress events**: use `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`
98	>    hooks (or whichever Claude Code hooks are documented for tool-call
99	>    boundaries at re-proposal time) to emit `tool_call` / `tool_result`
100	>    events during the turn. claude-p is batch (only `Stop`); Fizeau's
101	>    CONTRACT-004 requires intermediate `ProgressEvents` so this hook
102	>    set is load-bearing.
103	>
104	> 4. **Session lifetime**: **pooled long-lived sessions with `/clear`
105	>    between turns, lifetime bounded by the fiz process**. Rationale:
106	>    Ink + auth startup is the expensive part (~50–200 ms per claude-p's
107	>    measurements); amortizing it across the many Execute calls within
108	>    a single fiz invocation is worth the pool-management cost.
109	>    `/clear` resets conversation state without dropping the warm
110	>    session. The pool dies when fiz dies — no PID files, no daemon, no
111	>    cross-invocation persistence.
112	>
113	>    Pool key default: **per `(harness, workdir)`**. Claude sessions
114	>    are bound to a working directory at startup; switching workdirs in
115	>    an existing session is not supported by `claude`. Per-(harness)
116	>    only would force serialization across all workdirs;
117	>    per-(harness, workdir, model) is overkill — model selection is
118	>    cheap enough to run via `/model` post-`/clear`.
119	>
120	>    Pool depth default: **1 per key**. Adequate for serial agent
121	>    loops, which is the standalone CLI's usage. Service-mode
122	>    concurrency can raise this with no contract change.
123	>
124	>    Pool placement: the pool lives at package scope (a singleton in
125	>    `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/`) or at service scope (a
126	>    constructor-injected dependency on the Runner), **not as a field
127	>    on the Runner struct**. Two `&claudetui.Runner{}` instances must
128	>    share the pool, otherwise the dispatcher's "construct a fresh
129	>    Runner per Execute" pattern defeats the amortization. CONTRACT-004
130	>    invariant #6 forbids mutable quota/account state on the Runner
131	>    but does not forbid shared transport state behind a singleton;
132	>    this is the right escape valve.
133	>
134	> 5. **Empirical `/clear` semantics gate** (pre-implementation): verify
135	>    against the installed Claude Code that `/clear`:
136	>    - resets conversation history (the point of the command);
137	>    - does NOT reset model selection (otherwise per-turn `/model` is
138	>      required, lengthening the per-turn ritual);
139	>    - does NOT reset permission mode;
140	>    - does NOT close the auth/session token;
141	>    - starts a new transcript file at a path observable from the
142	>      next turn's `Stop` hook payload.
143	>
144	>    If any of those don't hold, the per-turn ritual lengthens but
145	>    the pool model is still worthwhile. If `/clear` doesn't exist or
146	>    is unstable in the installed version, fall back to per-Execute
147	>    sessions (claude-p model) and accept the cold-start cost.
148	>
149	> 6. **Orphan reaper**: fiz crashes leave pooled `claude` processes
150	>    orphaned. A startup reaper analogous to the existing
151	>    `service_stale_harness_reaper*.go` kills `claude` processes whose
152	>    parent fiz PID is gone, before the new fiz instance constructs
153	>    its pool. No persistent state across fiz invocations — the
154	>    reaper inspects live process state only.
155	>
156	> 7. **Hook conflict handling**: a user's existing
157	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` may declare its own `SessionStart` /
158	>    `Stop` / `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hooks. The `--settings
159	>    '<inline-json>'` mechanism's merge semantics (replace vs. layer)
160	>    are unspecified in claude-p's README and need explicit
161	>    verification before claude-tui can ship. If hooks are
162	>    replace-not-merge, Fizeau must compose with whatever the operator
163	>    already has, not stomp it.
164	>
165	> 8. **Subscription billing observation**: still required as a
166	>    promotion gate per ADR-014. Neither claude-p nor shannon claims
167	>    subscription billing; both route through the same `claude`
168	>    binary and inherit whatever billing classification that binary's
169	>    request paths produce. The re-proposal must include an empirical
170	>    measurement showing PTY+hooks-driven Claude moves the `/usage`
171	>    window, otherwise the fork's economic premise is unverified.
172	>
173	> ---
174	>
175	> The content below remains for historical reference of the original
176	> proposal.
177	
178	## Context
179	
180	The current `claude` harness (`internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go`) drives the
181	Claude CLI through `claude --print -p --output-format stream-json` (with a
182	legacy `--output-format json` fallback) via `os/exec`. That subprocess path
183	covers normal prompt execution today, but it is a different transport from the
184	direct PTY path Fizeau already uses for `/usage` quota probing
185	(`internal/harnesses/claude/quota_pty.go` over `internal/harnesses/ptyquota`,
186	`internal/pty/session`, `internal/pty/terminal`).
187	
188	**The driver for forking is Anthropic subscription pricing.** Claude Pro/Max
189	subscription capacity is billed against an account quota that is exposed
190	through the interactive Claude CLI surface (TUI + `/usage`). The Anthropic
191	API, including request paths a `claude --print` invocation may resolve
192	against, is metered separately at per-token API pricing. Routing prompt
193	execution through the interactive TUI is how Fizeau accesses subsidized
194	subscription capacity (ADR-011 cost-based routing already assumes this is
195	possible). The existing `claude --print` transport cannot be relied on to
196	keep landing on subscription capacity as Anthropic evolves the boundary; the
197	TUI surface is the durable, documented entry point for subscription quota.
198	
199	This is not about anti-automation fingerprinting or impersonating a human as
200	a security goal. It is about using the subscription product the way it is
201	priced, which means: drive the TUI, do not pass batch-API-shaped flags, and
202	do not introduce Fizeau-side signals (env vars, argv markers) that change
203	billing classification or invite policy enforcement against automated batch
204	use.
205	
206	ADR-002 already commits Fizeau to direct PTY ownership and bans tmux from the
207	core path. ADR-004 caps build vs. buy for the PTY library boundary. ADR-011
208	treats subsidized Claude/Codex quota as a routing-preferred capacity pool.
209	None of those ADRs specify *how* normal prompt execution should adopt PTY
210	without breaking the existing `claude` evidence base (cassettes, runner
211	tests, capability baseline rows, auto-routing eligibility).
212	
213	## Decision
214	
215	Fizeau will add a **new, separate primary harness identity `claude-tui`** that
216	implements the existing `harnesses.Harness` interface
217	(`internal/harnesses/types.go`, `Info`/`HealthCheck`/`Execute`) and runs the
218	Claude CLI exclusively through the direct PTY transport. `claude-tui` is a
219	fork — a sibling package alongside `internal/harnesses/claude/` — not a
220	mode, flag, or conditional branch in the existing runner.
221	
222	The existing `claude` harness keeps its current implementation, capability
223	evidence, and auto-routing eligibility unchanged. Both harnesses coexist
224	indefinitely; capability and routing decisions are tracked per-identity.
225	
226	`claude-tui` is the identity through which subscription-billed Claude
227	capacity is routed once it earns auto-routing eligibility. Until then, the
228	existing `claude` harness continues to serve routed Claude traffic.
229	
230	**Key Points**: separate package + registry identity | PTY only, no batch
231	flags, no Fizeau-side identification env/argv | both `claude` and
232	`claude-tui` are primary harnesses with independent baseline rows | both
233	implement the same `harnesses.Harness` interface.
234	
235	## Harness Interface (Normative)
236	
237	The new identity implements the existing, unchanged interface defined in
238	`internal/harnesses/types.go`:
239	
240	```go
241	type Harness interface {
242	    // Info returns identity + capability metadata for this harness.
243	    Info() HarnessInfo
244	
245	    // HealthCheck triggers a fresh probe (binary present, auth ok, etc.)
246	    // and returns nil if the harness is ready to execute.
247	    HealthCheck(ctx context.Context) error
248	
249	    // Execute runs one resolved request. Events stream on the returned
250	    // channel; a single final event closes the stream. The first error
251	    // return is reserved for setup failures (binary missing, etc.) — once
252	    // the channel is returned, all per-run failures are reported via a
253	    // final event with Status != "success".
254	    Execute(ctx context.Context, req ExecuteRequest) (<-chan Event, error)
255	}
256	```
257	
258	`HarnessInfo`, `ExecuteRequest`, `Event`, `FinalData`, `FinalUsage`,
259	`RoutingActual`, `ReasoningActual`, and the `EventType` closed union are
260	defined in the same file and are not extended by this ADR. CONTRACT-003 is
261	the public-surface contract that those internal shapes reflect; this ADR
262	adds no new event types, no new request fields, and no new metadata keys.
263	
264	`claude-tui` therefore differs from `claude` only in:
265	
266	- transport mechanism (PTY vs. `os/exec` batch),
267	- registry config (`HarnessConfig`) entry name, binary invocation, and
268	  baseline flags,
269	- `HarnessInfo.Name` returned by `Info()`,
270	- internal package layout and tests,
271	
272	not in interface, event shapes, or request semantics. A caller routing
273	through `harnesses.Harness` cannot tell the two apart except by the
274	`HarnessInfo.Name` it returns.
275	
276	A separate harness identity (rather than a `Transport` mode on a single
277	`HarnessConfig`) is required because:
278	
279	- `HarnessInfo.Name` is the key the capability matrix, routing layer, and
280	  evidence store use to attribute rows. Collapsing two transports into one
281	  name makes evidence ambiguous.
282	- `HarnessConfig` carries `BaseArgs`, `PermissionArgs`, `ModelFlag`,
283	  `ReasoningFlag`, and `TUIQuotaCommand` fields that have transport-specific
284	  meaning. A PTY harness uses none of `BaseArgs`/`ModelFlag`/`ReasoningFlag`

321	## Invocation Constraints
322	
323	These constraints derive from the subscription-pricing goal: invocation must
324	not look like batch-API automation, and Fizeau must not introduce side
325	channels that could be used to reclassify the request.
326	
327	`claude-tui` **must not**:
328	
329	- Pass any flag that signals batch/automation intent or selects a non-TUI
330	  output format: `--print`, `-p`, `--output-format`, `--stream-json`,
331	  `--effort`, `--model`, `--permission-mode`,
332	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, or any future Anthropic flag in the same
333	  family. Where a TUI affordance for the same setting exists (e.g. a `/model`
334	  selector), use that affordance via PTY input bytes. Where no TUI affordance
335	  exists, the capability is `gap` for `claude-tui` until one does — do not
336	  silently fall back to a CLI flag.
337	- Introduce Fizeau-side environment variables that identify the caller as an
338	  agent: no `CLAUDE_*`, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `*_AGENT*`, `*_AUTOMATED*`, or similar
339	  Fizeau-introduced names on this path. Pre-existing variables already set
340	  in the operator's environment are passed through unchanged via the
341	  documented allowlist below.
342	- Send single-keystroke input bursts faster than the configured inter-key
343	  delay band (default 25–75ms per logical key). Pasted prompts go through
344	  bracketed paste and may arrive as one burst; that matches real paste
345	  behavior and is allowed.
346	
347	`claude-tui` **may**:
348	
349	- Use the bracketed-paste sequence to deliver a multi-line prompt in one
350	  event. Bracketed paste is the documented terminal mechanism for paste
351	  input and is what a real paste produces.
352	- Read raw PTY bytes, derive frames through `internal/pty/terminal`, and
353	  emit Fizeau service events from them. Service-event emission is internal
354	  to Fizeau and is not visible to the Claude binary.
355	- Cancel a turn with the key combination the TUI documents for cancellation
356	  (Esc by default; Ctrl-C as a fallback that exits the session, in which
357	  case `claude-tui` restarts a session for the next request).
358	- Reuse the existing `internal/pty/cassette` recorder and

424	## Performance and Cost Acknowledgement
425	
426	The fork is not free:
427	
428	- **Parsing cost**: Frame derivation through `internal/pty/terminal`
429	  (vt10x-backed) on every spinner/render update is meaningfully more
430	  expensive than parsing `stream-json` JSONL lines. For long turns with
431	  many redraws the CPU and wall-clock cost is noticeable. The benchmark
432	  suite (`scripts/benchmark/`) must include a `claude-tui` lane so this
433	  cost is measured before promotion to auto-routing.
434	- **Per-turn latency**: Inter-key delays for menu navigation add a fixed
435	  overhead (commonly a few hundred ms total) per turn that selects
436	  model/reasoning. Bracketed-paste prompts do not add latency.
437	- **Code duplication**: Two runners, two parsers, two discovery paths, two
438	  cassette suites. Estimated 1500–2500 LOC of additional code carried
439	  indefinitely (the existing `claude` package is ~3.5k LOC across
440	  runner/stream/quota; `claude-tui` will be smaller because it skips the
441	  stream-json fallback path and the `--print` argument builder). Review
442	  burden is the larger long-term cost.
443	
444	These costs are accepted because subscription pricing is the load-bearing
445	economic constraint for primary-routing Claude capacity (ADR-011). If
446	`claude --print` ever lands on subscription capacity reliably and durably
447	without TUI-driven traffic, this ADR is open to revision.
